headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify unsafe outputs from the content-writing agent into leakage, conflicts, and downstream errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing agent with no documented isolation or input surfaces, while open-webui supports MCP, plugins, and tool calling plus broad network/file access. The pair has a plausible bridge if A’s content is copied into B or B ingests A-generated text as instructions; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF open-webui ingests content from awesome-cli-apps via copy-paste, files, or MCP tools
IF open-webui treats A-generated text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic tool execution in open-webui
Use a strict prompt delimiter for any imported text
Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Review any A-generated content before pasting into B
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly touches files, mounted volumes, API keys, and multiple external APIs, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, B can expose A-originated content or secrets to third parties; the evidence is docs-only, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same local files or mounted volume
IF open-webui is configured with external API connectors while handling A-produced documents or secrets
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Remove API keys from shared directories
Turn off unused external connectors in open-webui
Store A outputs in a non-sensitive scratch folder
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-cli-apps is not runnable, so direct write contention is not evidenced, but open-webui supports persistent shared sessions, multiple instances, and Redis-backed state. If the pair is orchestrated to share mutable resources, open-webui’s concurrency model can conflict with A-produced artifacts or edits; uncertainty prevents a lower rating.
conditions: IF open-webui instances share the same Redis-backed session state
IF both agents write to the same mounted files or shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate session namespaces
Avoid shared writable directories
Serialize writes through one operator
Disable multi-instance sharing for the test
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act on tool outputs, browse, and call APIs, so if it consumes A-generated content as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into external actions or user-visible artifacts. awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing source, and the pair lacks any documented verification gate, making the default pathway dangerous.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards A-generated text into tools, browsers, or API calls without verification
IF A-produced content is treated as factual input by B
mitigations: Require human review before tool use
Add a verification step for all A-originated claims
Disable browser and API actions for imported content
Use citations-only rendering for A outputs
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, documents, notes, calendar events, and persistent memory, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress. Even without a documented residency mismatch, the pair can move regulated or sensitive data into third-party services through B’s connectors, so compliance risk is material but not proven critical.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed through open-webui connectors
IF data retention or residency requirements apply to the shared content
mitigations: Restrict sensitive data from open-webui
Disable external connectors for regulated workloads
Review retention settings before use
Keep API keys out of imported documents
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
